name: Computer Control
description: Controls Windows applications and the desktop using app discovery, window management, screenshots, and mouse/keyboard input. For accurate visual target coordinates, use find_screen_coordinates, which delegates to the saved Screen Coordinate Finder agent and Mocu's full-monitor vision workflow; screenshot_app is window-only and must not be used to derive desktop coordinates.

commands.title: Find screen coordinates with Screen Coordinate Finder
commands.description: Delegate screen-element location to the saved Screen Coordinate Finder agent, which uses Mocu's full-primary-monitor desktop_vision_action screenshot and exact monitor bounds. Input: {"target":"Search box","action":"click"}; omit action for coordinates only. You may instead pass {"request":"..."} as a complete task. Do not use screenshot_app to locate screen elements; its window image is unsuitable for desktop coordinates. The agent returns English JSON and can perform a requested mouse action through Computer Control.

commands.title: Check whether an app is open
commands.description: Input a program name such as Chrome or Notepad. Returns matching processes, PIDs, and visible window titles. Accepts a string or {"name":"Chrome"}.

commands.title: Control an application window
commands.description: Open, minimize, maximize, focus/restore, or gracefully close a Windows app. Example: {"action":"focus","name":"Google Chrome"}.

commands.title: Get application window state
commands.description: Report whether a matching app window is minimized, maximized, normal, currently foreground/focused, and on the primary monitor. Input: {"name":"Google Chrome"}. Returns monitor and work-area bounds for each matching window.

commands.title: Capture an application window screenshot
commands.description: Capture only the named app window as PNG and save it. It does not provide reliable desktop coordinates. Use find_screen_coordinates to locate screen elements via the full-monitor vision agent, not this window screenshot. Uses a small screen-icon desktop notification when capture begins; it auto-dismisses after 10 seconds.

commands.title: Control desktop mouse and keyboard
commands.description: Move/click/scroll the Windows desktop mouse or send keyboard input. Coordinates x/y are physical virtual-desktop pixels (including negative monitor origins); use the exact origin and dimensions from the full-monitor screenshot metadata. For scroll, use {"action":"scroll","direction":"vertical","delta":-120,"x":500,"y":300} to scroll down at a point in the scrollable page content; use positive delta (e.g. 120) to scroll up. delta is a non-zero integer from -1200 to 1200 in Windows wheel units; default is +120 (up). x and y must be provided together; if omitted, scrolling occurs at the current pointer position. To reach the bottom of a long page, scroll down in repeated calls, checking a fresh screenshot after each call and stopping when the bottom is visible; success means the wheel input was sent, not that the page reached its bottom. Supports move, click, scroll, press_key, hotkey, and type_text. The extension explicitly reads and writes Mocu JSON-RPC streams as UTF-8, so type_text receives exact Unicode input regardless of the Windows system code page. It sends text as ordered UTF-16 Unicode keyboard events, independent of the active keyboard layout. Before mouse move/click/scroll, shows a styled desktop notice asking the user not to interact; it auto-dismisses after 5 seconds.
